svg.title: Better Theater Mode
svg.desc: On YouTube, theater.js watches YouTube's player for its own theater attribute and sets classes on the page that theater.css uses to make the player fill the whole window. On every other site, generic.js reacts to the T key, Esc or the site's theater button: it finds the biggest video, and pins the player box to the window with inline styles. Inside an embedded player frame, generic.js passes keys up to the page's copy and is told to fill or unfill. The popup saves settings to chrome.storage.sync, which both scripts read. YouTube theater button: YouTube's player → theater.js + .css → YouTube's player. T on another site: You → generic.js → Site's player box. T inside an embedded player: generic.js in the player iframe → generic.js → Site's player box, generic.js in the player iframe.
